sources.shortCitation: Der glückliche Herr Fünf advertisement — Der Kinematograph
sources.fullCitation: [Advertisement for Der glückliche Herr Fünf]. Der Kinematograph (Berlin), August 1932, scan leaf 118. Internet Archive / Media History Digital Library.
sources.repository: Internet Archive / Media History Digital Library
sources.researchNote: The advertisement uses the pre-release title Der glückliche Herr Fünf, after Alice Berend’s novel Herr Fünf. It credits Heinz Hilpert as director, Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann with the music, Willi Domgraf-Fassbaender in the leading role, and Pax Film GmbH as producer. The released film is documented elsewhere as Ich will Dich Liebe lehren.

sources.shortCitation: “Paramount’s Joinville studio, in France, has hit a new high in activity” — Variety, 26 September 1933
sources.fullCitation: [Paramount’s Joinville studio.] News item. Variety, 26 September 1933. Media History Digital Library, Variety vol. 111; digitised by the Internet Archive.
sources.title: Paramount’s Joinville studio — Variety, 26 September 1933
sources.researchNote: The item reports that all four sound stages of “Paramount’s Joinville studio” were occupied and booked ahead by French and American companies, and names among them Fred Bacos, finishing the second of two films for Fox, and Erich Pommer, “preparing to begin shooting his first of three more for Fox”, before adding “Also in work at Joinville are dub jobs”. Pommer’s Fox-Europa unit had finished Liliom; the next film it made was On a volé un homme, with music by Jurmann and Kaper.

sources.repository: Internet Archive / Media History Digital Library

sources.fullCitation: “Pommer Out of Hospital But Fox-Europa Quiet.” Paris, 18 January. Variety, 23 January 1934. Media History Digital Library, Variety vol. 113; digitised by the Internet Archive.
sources.title: Pommer Out of Hospital But Fox-Europa Quiet — Variety, 1934
sources.researchNote: Reports that Fox-Europa’s first two pictures, Liliom and On a volé un homme, were finished, and that the unit “will probably get going again along in March at the Paramount Joinville studio”.

sources.title: Ciné-Miroir, 12 October 1934 — the two studios called Joinville
